central_question: After a visible floral trait is lost, does its future regain necessarily reconstruct the ancestral pigment, gene regulator, ecological function, and heritable phenotype together?

definitions.visible_regain: Flower pigment or pattern becomes observable again after inferred or experimentally documented absence; not necessarily restoring ancestral hue
definitions.ancestral_hue_restoration: Present pigment phenotype matches published inferred pre-loss ancestral dominant hue, rather than simply a return to any visible anthocyanin
definitions.regulator_reuse: Original functional regulator repaired or redeployed, distinct from an alternate functional paralog
definitions.family_homology: Short original-RNA/GenBank sequence similarity; not enzyme activity or intact whole genomic pathway
definitions.independent_evolutionary_origin: Separate reconstructed phylogenetic return event; multiple studies of the same clade/tip are not independent
definitions.fitness: Direct fecundity/viability/ecological-function result measured under a relevant comparative or experimental control

cases.source_ancestry: Colourless ancestor supported by published phylogeny, not experimentally observed ancestral flowers
cases.focal_molecular_mechanism: Compensatory two-base deletion restored AN2 coding frame/function
cases.caveat: Same Petunia radiation as P. exserta; do not count studies/species as independent plant-clade replications

cases.focal_molecular_mechanism: AN2 nonfunctional; functional DPL paralog upregulated in petal limb, plus hydroxylation and acylation changes
cases.pigment_tissue_evidence: LC-MS flower anthocyanins and floral genetic expression/functional interventions
cases.caveat: Petunia secreta and exserta are different published mechanisms but still ONE genus; red hue is not pelargonidin synthesis

cases.source_ancestry: Published dated/phylogenetic analysis places tip in old unpigmented A clade; direction is inferred
cases.focal_molecular_mechanism: Published flower-bud cDNA structural sequences; late F3'5'h, Dfr, Ans flower expression regained relative to unpigmented A clade; specific causal regulatory allele not resolved
cases.pigment_tissue_evidence: Published flower HPLC cyanidin and seven-gene comparative expression
cases.caveat: Ho 2016 and Larter 2018 overlap the SAME Iochrominae clade; phenotype return and late expression jointly do not establish causally retained regulator

cases.source_ancestry: Experimental transposon insertion/excision within cultivated genotype; not dated ancient whole-flower pigment loss
cases.focal_molecular_mechanism: CACTA transposable-element excision restored suppressive ELUTA MYB activity; S1 22 magenta versus 5 pale and S2 segregating
cases.pigment_tissue_evidence: Transposon-tagging, phenotype, repressor assays, two-generation inheritance
cases.caveat: Functionally documented regulatory reversibility is not independent angiosperm evidence of ancient floral anthocyanin regain

cases.source_ancestry: Published floral colour attenuation associated with regulatory translation change, no regained event
cases.focal_molecular_mechanism: Upstream translation-initiation alteration in 5-prime UTR of PELAN reduces activator translation
cases.caveat: Do not recode a mechanism of phenotype loss as a failed experiment to re-express it

cases.source_ancestry: No supported loss-then-regain polarity for individual colour contrast
cases.focal_molecular_mechanism: Original six 2026 young-leaf first-R1 prefixes, 747234 reads, 215 selected source-fragments after competition with 104890 C. japonicum transcript sequences; TR39766 and TR41106 fragments in 6/6 source libraries
cases.caveat: Leaf RNA homology fragments are not functional enzyme assignments, flower gene expression, genotype persistence or phenotype regain

biological_target_next: Estimate separately Pr(any biochemical reexpression), Pr(ancestral biochemical branch restored | reexpression), Pr(heritable persistence) and ecological fitness on validated whole-clade heldouts; current selected literature does not estimate these probabilities.
publication_boundary: Forni et al 2026 reviews lost-trait reversals/novelty; existence of multiple routes is known. This is a source-audited hypothesis registry, not a newly tested general evolutionary law.
